Modals

Dialog boxes and confirmation sheets, styled for RoutePlate.

Use a modal for a dialog box, a confirmation, or other content that should sit above the page. RoutePlate styles a native <dialog class="modal">. Open it with showModal() and close it with close() — the Dialog API, not a JavaScript plugin.

<button type="button" class="btn filled" onclick="document.getElementById('modal1').showModal()">
  Show
</button>

<dialog id="modal1" class="modal">
  <div class="modal-header">
    <h4>Modal Header</h4>
  </div>
  <div class="modal-content">
    <p>A bunch of text</p>
  </div>
  <form method="dialog" class="modal-footer">
    <button type="submit" class="btn text">Disagree</button>
    <button type="submit" class="btn filled">Agree</button>
  </form>
</dialog>

A <form method="dialog"> in the footer closes the dialog when a submit button is pressed. modal-close only sets a pointer cursor — it does not close anything by itself.

Initialization

No plugin init is required. The stylesheet is written for a native <dialog> with the open attribute and a ::backdrop.

RoutePlate.Modal is still exported, and AutoInit() still matches .modal, but that class is a rewrite in progress: open() and close() are empty. Use the Dialog API on the element instead. 

const modal = document.querySelector('#modal1');
modal.showModal();
modal.close();

Methods

Call these on the <dialog> element. See the HTMLDialogElement documentation for the full API.

.showModal();

Open the dialog as a modal, with a backdrop.

modal.showModal();
.close();

Close the dialog.

modal.close();

Customization

The dialog reads these custom properties. Override them on .modal if you need different padding or a different surface.

Property Role
--modal-border-radius Corner radius (default 28px).
--modal-padding Header and footer padding (default 24px).
--modal-padding-bottom Extra space under the header title (default 16px).
--modal-background-color Surface tint used for the dialog, header, and footer.

Bottom Sheet Modals

Add bottom-sheet for a shorter dialog with square bottom corners. It is still a native <dialog> — open it the same way.

Modal Header

Bottom sheet modals are useful for a short list of actions. They use the same header, content, and footer structure as a regular modal.

 
<button type="button" class="btn tonal" onclick="document.getElementById('modal2').showModal()">
  Show Bottom Sheet
</button>

<dialog id="modal2" class="modal bottom-sheet">
  <div class="modal-header">
    <h4>Modal Header</h4>
  </div>
  <div class="modal-content">
    <p>A bunch of text</p>
  </div>
</dialog>
